headline: Enhancer and CTCF maps link chromatin accessibility to gene regulation
label: Chromatin Regulatory Element Mapping
summary: Single-nucleus and multi-omics resources are sharpening how candidate enhancers and CTCF sites are linked to gene regulation.
synthesis: The common thread is the mapping of regulatory DNA from chromatin accessibility data, with emphasis on resolving enhancer-gene links and the determinants of occupancy. A single-nucleus atlas profiles 1.17M candidate cis-regulatory elements across 104k prenatal cortical nuclei from 54 donors, while CREMAP removes shared latent technical and biological variation before testing peak-gene links in single-cell multi-omics. Sequence-to-function models and E2GScore are benchmarked for enhancer-gene interaction inference, and a CTCF framework identifies five mechanisms of variable occupancy across hundreds of cell and tissue types. Large-scale ATAC-seq comparisons show that text metadata embeddings weakly track chromatin similarity, and GTRD 2026 extends uniformly processed regulatory data resources. What is new is the attention to confounding and benchmarking in enhancer-gene inference rather than a single shared biological finding, as the items differ in scope.
